learning: Hypotheses: the s-bend jitter (steering_oscillation 0.37) limits bend performance, so more kd would help if measured separately. The slalom line loss of 2.0 is a control-response limit. Completion_time on the oval shows whether base_speed can rise.
notes: Delivers the iteration-10 controller unchanged on the Builder's iteration-10 geometry. The measured 546.4 result is the only evidence for this design, and an untested gain change would risk the unseen-track score.
rationale: The final race is scored on an unseen track, so this package keeps the best measured controller rather than testing an untried gain. The best raced design is iteration 10 (546.4), built on the iteration-9 geometry. Its controller (base_speed 1.0, kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.6, last_direction) is the one I deliver. Iteration 10 finished the oval 20 of 20 at 1.90 s mean, so the speed margin is adequate. The s-bend reached 9 of 20 finishes with line_loss_events 1.5, down from 2.3 at iteration 9, and steering_oscillation 0.37. The slalom still lost the line in all 20 runs (line_loss_events 2.0, down from 2.1). The Builder has held the geometry unchanged at the iteration-10 values, so the controller is the only variable and the geometry matches the evidence. I considered raising kd further to damp the s-bend jitter (0.37). That is the main remaining lever, but its effect is untested, and the kd and base_speed changes were made together, so I cannot attribute the gain to either. Changing an unmeasured gain on the final unseen track could cost score with no later race to correct it. I therefore keep the measured controller. Expected result: a score close to the iteration-10 level, about 546, on the development tracks. I make no claim about the unseen track.
